weather_options.recession: Jobs are harder to keep and markets fall: job-loss probability x3, no real wage growth, portfolio returns 15 points/year lower during the window.
weather_options.inflation: Prices rise faster than planned while wages keep their usual pace: purchasing power drops.
weather_options.market_crash: Invested savings lose a share of their value in one month, then markets behave as usual.
weather_options.job_loss: Income stops for a few months; unemployment insurance replaces part of it (see assumption AS-unemployment-replacement).

assumptions.label: Average annual inflation (CPI)
assumptions.source: FSO CPI annual averages: +2.1% (2023), +1.1% (2024), +0.2% (2025) (https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/prices/consumer-price-index.html). SNB defines price stability as 0-2% and kept its policy rate at 0% on 24 Sep 2026 (https://www.snb.ch/en/publications/communication/press-releases-restricted/pre_20260924). 1% = mid-point of the SNB range, close to the 2023-2025 average (1.1%)

assumptions.label: Year-to-year volatility of inflation
assumptions.source: Modelling choice sized on the spread of recent FSO annual CPI changes (2.1%, 1.1%, 0.2% for 2023-2025; same FSO link as AS-inflation-mean)

assumptions.label: Real wage growth per year (on top of inflation)
assumptions.source: FSO Swiss Wage Index: real wages +1.6% in 2025 and +0.7% in 2024, after three years of decline (FSO release April 2026, https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/work-income/wages-income-employment-labour-costs/wage-index.html). 1% is a modelling choice: economy-wide averages are lower, young workers usually progress faster

assumptions.label: Assumed annual return of a balanced portfolio (nominal, after fees)
assumptions.source: Pictet 'Performance of Swiss shares and bonds 1926-2024': Swiss shares 7.7%/year, Swiss bonds 4.0%/year nominal; a 60/40 mix about 6% since 1900 (https://www.pictet.com/content/dam/www/documents/publications/shares-and-bonds-in-switzerland/2025/PWM_Performance-Swiss-shares-and-bonds-EN.pdf). We use a more prudent 4% for a 50/50 mix after ~0.5% fees, because CHF bond yields are now near zero; past returns do not guarantee future ones

assumptions.label: Annual volatility of the balanced portfolio
assumptions.source: Modelling choice (typical order of magnitude for a 50/50 equity/bond mix); not checked against a published series

assumptions.label: Interest on positive cash (savings account)
assumptions.source: Average Swiss savings account rate 0.11% (Jan 2026, 133 offers) and 0.12% (Feb 2026), Moneyland.ch (https://www.moneyland.ch/en/interest-rates-savings-analysis-january-2026); SNB policy rate 0% (https://www.snb.ch)

assumptions.label: Probability of losing the job in a given year
assumptions.source: SECO registered unemployment rate 2.9-3.0% in mid-2026, peak 3.2% in Feb 2026 (https://www.seco.admin.ch, https://www.amstat.ch). Using the unemployment rate as the yearly probability of a job loss is a modelling simplification

assumptions.label: Average length of an unemployment spell
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified; SECO publishes registered durations at https://www.amstat.ch. Unemployment insurance pays at most 520 daily allowances (https://www.arbeit.swiss)

assumptions.label: Share of income kept while unemployed (unemployment insurance)
assumptions.source: Swiss unemployment insurance pays 70% of the insured salary; 80% with dependent children under 25, an insured salary below CHF 3,797/month, or a disability of 40%+ (https://www.arbeit.swiss/secoalv/en/home/menue/stellensuchende/arbeitslos-was-tun-/finanzielles.html). Requires 12 months of contributions: students without them get 0

assumptions.label: Probability per year of an unexpected expense (health, repairs, family)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice with no source: illustrates that budgets get surprises

assumptions.label: Average size of an unexpected expense
assumptions.source: Modelling choice with no source: about one month of a student's expenses

assumptions.label: Income tax level (1 = illustrative Lausanne table)
assumptions.table_unit: [annual net salary CHF (after social contributions, at today's prices), effective rate]
assumptions.source: Illustrative effective federal+cantonal+communal rate, single person, Lausanne (VD), no church tax. Cross-checked only against a third-party calculator (cantonal CHF 3,216 + communal CHF 1,629 at CHF 50,000 gross, https://ch.talent.com/en/tax-calculator/Waadt) and Lausanne's 2026 multipliers (canton 155%, commune 78.5%, https://www.lausanne.ch/officiel/administration/finances-et-mobilite/finances/impots/coefficient-taux-arrete-imposition.html). Not verified with the official ESTV calculator (https://swisstaxcalculator.estv.admin.ch)

assumptions.label: Sell investments automatically when cash goes negative (1 = yes)
assumptions.source: Modelling rule (no external source): a shortfall is first covered by selling investments; any remaining negative cash is an unfunded financing need, not an assumed loan (UBS starter-kit convention)

assumptions.label: Emergency reserve considered healthy
assumptions.source: Rule of thumb (3-6 months of expenses), a value judgement not verified against a source

assumptions.label: Debt payments above this share of income are considered stretched
assumptions.source: Rule of thumb inspired by the Swiss 'one third of income' affordability practice; illustrative, not a lending policy, not verified

assumptions.label: Employee AHV/IV/EO contribution (share of gross salary)
assumptions.source: BSV synoptic table of contribution rates, state 1 Jan 2026: employee AHV 4.35% + IV 0.7% + EO 0.25% = 5.3% (same for the employer) (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf); PwC Social security key figures 2026 (https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Employee unemployment insurance (ALV) contribution
assumptions.source: 1.1% employee share on salary up to CHF 148,200/year, 2026 (BSV synoptic table https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf; PwC 2026 https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Insured-salary cap for ALV and accident insurance
assumptions.source: Maximum insured salary CHF 148,200/year, 2026 (BSV synoptic table https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf; PwC 2026 https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Employee non-occupational accident insurance (NBU)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified: NBU premiums are set by each insurer and sector and deducted from the employee up to the insured-salary cap; 1% is an illustrative middle value

assumptions.label: BVG (pillar 2) entry threshold
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: entry threshold CHF 22,680, unchanged in 2026 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG coordination deduction
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: coordination deduction CHF 26,460 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG upper salary limit
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: upper limit of the insured salary CHF 90,720 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG minimum coordinated salary
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: minimum coordinated salary CHF 3,780 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 25-34 (share of coordinated salary)
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG age credits 7% / 10% / 15% / 18% for ages 25-34 / 35-44 / 45-54 / 55-65 (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16); the BVG 21 reform that would have changed them was rejected

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 35-44
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 45-54
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 55-65
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: Employee share of the BVG age credits
assumptions.source: Rule: the employer pays at least half of the contributions (Art. 66 BVG); 0.5 = the legal minimum split, many pension funds pay more (modelling choice)

assumptions.label: BVG minimum interest on mandatory savings
assumptions.source: Federal Council kept the BVG minimum interest rate at 1.25% for 2026 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/de/altersvorsorge-beruflichen-vorsorge)

assumptions.label: Net salary if she starts working now
assumptions.source: UBS LauzHack starter kit scenario_config.json ('Start working'), illustrative. Checked against the starter kit file; the figure itself is illustrative, not market data

assumptions.label: Rent of a studio in Lausanne
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified: starter-kit total expenses CHF 3,000 split by the team into rent CHF 1,100 + other CHF 1,900

assumptions.label: Master's tuition and study costs per year
assumptions.source: UBS starter kit (CHF 2,500 at months 0 and 12, tuition plus study costs). Low end: EPFL invoice CHF 780/semester = CHF 1,560/year (tuition CHF 730 + fees) for students with a Swiss entry qualification; foreign students subject to the tripled fee pay CHF 2,240/semester (https://www.epfl.ch/education/studies/tuition-fee-other-fees/). High end: UBS synthetic scenario-assumptions.csv annual_tuition_chf=8000 for P00001

assumptions.label: Student job income during the master's
assumptions.source: UBS starter kit ('Master's degree' phase 1) and synthetic-profiles.csv reference income. Checked against the starter kit file; the figure itself is illustrative, not market data

assumptions.label: Net salary after the master's
assumptions.source: UBS starter kit ('Master's degree' phase 2), illustrative. Checked against the starter kit file; the figure itself is illustrative, not market data

assumptions.label: Net salary abroad (converted to CHF)
assumptions.source: UBS starter kit ('Move abroad'), illustrative; exchange rate held constant. Checked against the starter kit file; the figure itself is illustrative, not market data

assumptions.label: One-off cost of moving abroad
assumptions.source: UBS starter kit ('Move abroad' one-off cost). Checked against the starter kit file; the figure itself is illustrative, not market data

assumptions.label: Rent of a flat abroad, alone
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. UBS starter kit total 'Move abroad' expenses split by the team; to verify with Eurostat/Destatis rent statistics for the chosen city.

assumptions.label: Negotiated raise on the first salary (about 5%)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. About 5% of CHF 4,200; to verify with the FSO Swiss Earnings Structure Survey, https://www.bfs.admin.ch (salary progression by age).

assumptions.label: Raise after a promotion in year 3 (about 15%)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. About 15% of CHF 4,200; to verify with the FSO Swiss Earnings Structure Survey, https://www.bfs.admin.ch.

assumptions.label: Assumed annual return of an 80% equity portfolio
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. Pictet 1926-2024 study (Swiss shares about 7.7%/year nominal) minus fees and a margin of prudence.

assumptions.label: Volatility of an 80% equity portfolio
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. Modelling choice between the balanced portfolio (10%) and a pure equity index (about 17%).

assumptions.label: Resale value of the car after 2 years
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. About 50% depreciation after 2 years; to verify with a used-car price index.

assumptions.label: Side job income
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. A few hours a week at a student-job rate; to verify.

assumptions.label: Income from a 60% job while studying
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. 60% of the CHF 4,200 junior salary; a student at 60% may earn less. To verify.

assumptions.label: Income from an 80% job while studying
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. 80% of the CHF 4,200 junior salary; feasibility next to studies is itself a modelling choice.

assumptions.label: Interest rate of the study loan
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with Vaud cantonal study grants and loans (Office cantonal des bourses d'études), https://www.vd.ch.

assumptions.label: Scholarship during the master's
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with Vaud cantonal study grants and loans (Office cantonal des bourses d'études), https://www.vd.ch or the EPFL social scholarship (https://www.epfl.ch/education/studies/en/epfl-social-scholarship/).

assumptions.label: Paid internship in the second year
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with EPFL internship guidelines or a Swiss salary survey.

assumptions.label: Raise after a promotion abroad in year 3 (about 15%)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. About 15% of CHF 3,700; to verify.

assumptions.label: Income from a side project
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. Illustrative; a side project may earn nothing.

assumptions.label: Net salary after a later master's, with experience
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with the FSO Swiss Earnings Structure Survey, https://www.bfs.admin.ch.

assumptions.label: Net salary of a job in Zurich, with experience
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with the FSO Swiss Earnings Structure Survey, https://www.bfs.admin.ch by region.

assumptions.label: Rent of a studio in Zurich
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified. To verify with FSO rent statistics by canton.
